scope.description: In three trials per call kind, issue 128 VerifyLeader, Barrier or Apply calls while Shutdown is interleaved into the fill, count how many of those futures are still incomplete 4000ms later, then issue 8 further calls of the same kind after Shutdown has returned and record whether each is answered within 500ms; a no-shutdown control runs the same call kinds without ever shutting down. Each case emits an assurance_shutdown_setup event and an assurance_shutdown_result event carrying the counts, the outcome histograms for both phases and the shutdown error.
assumptions: VerifyLeader is a legal call at any time, including after Shutdown, and the documented generic error for that case is ErrRaftShutdown, which the API's own select returns when the shutdown channel is chosen.
A single-voter node removes commit latency as a confounder and makes every call complete in well under a millisecond while the node is running.
The 4000ms window is long enough that a future answered only by the exited run loop would show as incomplete; nothing else in the harness can answer these futures.
excluded: A BatchApplyCh configuration, where applyCh becomes buffered and the apply path should behave like the verify path; and multi-node variants.

basis.prefix: Each case starts one real Raft instance in this process with its own InmemStore, InmemSnapshotStore and InmemTransport, bootstrapped as a single Voter with HeartbeatTimeout = ElectionTimeout = LeaderLeaseTimeout = 50ms, and waits until it reports Leader. It emits assurance_shutdown_setup, then issues 128 calls of the chosen kind from separate goroutines, each waiting on Error() with a 4000ms deadline and recording whether it returned and with which error. In the shutdown cases a goroutine sleeps 2ms and then calls Shutdown(), so the fill and the exit overlap; the case waits for Shutdown to return, then issues 8 further calls of the same kind one at a time, each waiting 500ms, and records their outcomes; finally it waits for all per-call timers and emits assurance_shutdown_result with the returned, stuck and post-phase counts, the outcome histograms, the shutdown error and the node state. The no-shutdown control never calls Shutdown. The harness is TestAssuranceShutdownFutureCompletion.

comparisons.description: VerifyLeader after Shutdown returned: at least one of the eight post-shutdown calls was still unanswered after 500ms. Holds means the predicted strand was observed on a call that has no race with the shutdown itself.
Barrier after Shutdown returned: the contrast case, expected to answer every post-shutdown call with the shutdown error because its channel is unbuffered by default.
Apply after Shutdown returned: same contrast as Barrier.
VerifyLeader control without shutdown: no call is left incomplete when nothing is shutting down.

before.description: Issue 64 VerifyLeader, Barrier or Apply calls in parallel against a freshly started single-voter node while Shutdown runs concurrently, count how many of those futures have not completed 400ms after Shutdown has returned, and compare with the same call kinds issued on a node that is never shut down. Each case emits an assurance_shutdown_setup event and an assurance_shutdown_result event carrying the counts, the outcome histogram and the shutdown error.
assumptions: A single-voter node is a supported configuration and makes each call complete quickly when the node is running, so any incomplete future is attributable to the shutdown race rather than to slow commit.
64 concurrent calls per trial is a probe of exposure, not a rate estimate; the concurrency is what makes the race observable.
Waiting 400ms after Shutdown() has returned is enough for any future that can still be answered, because the run loop has already exited by then.
excluded: Whether a stuck future can be recovered by any other API, and any multi-node variant where a future could still be answered by another goroutine after shutdown.

before.description: VerifyLeader against a concurrent shutdown: at least one future never completed. Holds means the predicted hang was observed.
VerifyLeader control without shutdown: no future is left incomplete, so incompleteness is not a property of the probe itself.
Barrier against a concurrent shutdown: whether the same hang appears on the apply-channel path, which the harness drains in batches.
Apply against a concurrent shutdown: whether the same hang appears for command application.

after.description: VerifyLeader after Shutdown returned: at least one of the eight post-shutdown calls was still unanswered after 500ms. Holds means the predicted strand was observed on a call that has no race with the shutdown itself.
Barrier after Shutdown returned: the contrast case, expected to answer every post-shutdown call with the shutdown error because its channel is unbuffered by default.
Apply after Shutdown returned: same contrast as Barrier.
VerifyLeader control without shutdown: no call is left incomplete when nothing is shutting down.

revision_reason: The first run left the trigger timing dependent (9, 41 and 0 stranded futures across three trials) and waited only 1500ms per call, so the revision lengthens the completion window to 4000ms, raises the call count to 128, interleaves Shutdown 2ms into the fill, and adds a post-shutdown phase that issues 8 calls of the same kind after Shutdown has returned and records which of them are answered promptly. No measured field was removed and the event names are unchanged.
